decisions.quote: The findings broadly confirm the results of Susac et al.; that is, physics students perform better than nonphysics students. While economics students likely have better prior knowledge on finance context than psychology students, the physics students still outperform them on the finance questions. In contrast to the work by Susac et al., both groups of students had the same visit duration on the graphs, consequently proving total dwell time to be an inadequate predictor of performance.
decisions.reason: While the authors confirm Susac et al.'s finding that physics students outperform nonphysics students (as well as several item-level viewing-time effects), that confirmation is explicitly tied to the performance comparison rather than an overall verdict superseding other tested comparisons. Because the authors explicitly contrast their results with Susac et al. regarding group differences in graph visit duration (and question-type effects among physics students), the replication outcome is mixed.
